transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-09-30
- Start: 14:00 PDT
- Duration: 47m
- Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connell (Nimbus SRE), Sofia Park (Nimbus ML), Grace Huang (Nimbus Security), Owen Tran (Nimbus Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on connectivity/provisioning status, early benchmark artifacts, KV cache tuning, and security signoffs. Agreed to run focused microbenchmarks and exchange security artifacts; staging peering is gating some runs.

Topics:
- Staging VPC peering and firewall rules
- KMS/HSM expectations and data residency
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs: batch vs streaming
- KV cache warmup strategy and prefix caching
- Next steps: benchmarks, docs, and a deeper SE-led tuning session

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this to 45 minutes, got a handful of items: staging peering status, bench results, and some tuning notes. how's the staging peering looking, Liam?
[00:12] Liam: Yeah hi Ethan, uh, quick update — we started the peering request last week, it's in the cloud ops queue, we had to adjust some egress rules. should be done early next week but, uh, there's a firewall rule for outbound to 10.4.0.0/16 that we still need to open.
[00:28] Priya: Cool. that's the one that blocks the control-plane and the KV connections; without it we can run only local mocks which won't show the real we saw on prod.
[00:40] Sofia: Right — we ran a quick smoke test with local stubs; latency looked okay but cost wasn't representative, so we'd prefer the real peered path.
[00:51] Grace: from security we want to confirm that keys stay in our KMS — we can't have redwood-managed keys for this pilot. also need SOC2 excerpt and any audit log retention details.
[01:05] Carlos: Grace — that's totally reasonable. Ethan and I will pull the security pack and highlight the KMS/HSM notes. we'll flag which flows require customer-managed KMS.
[01:16] Ethan: to set expectations, hosted endpoints can work with customer-managed encryption via our KMS integration, but the dedicated appliance gives you control over HSM-backed keys if you need them. there is a small ops delta in dedicated, roughly 8–12% additional setup time but more isolation.
[01:34] Owen: curious on numbers — that 8–12% is what exactly? latency penalty, cost, or hours?
[01:40] Ethan: sorry, poor phrasing — setup/ops overhead. In terms of runtime performance, dedicated can run slightly faster for sustained throughput because of pinned GPUs, but cost varies with utilization. we'll share a small pricing delta spreadsheet after the call.
[01:55] Priya: on the tuning side we've been looking at KV cache warmup: if your prompts have a high prefix reuse we can get big tail latency wins. the trick is sequence length distribution — are you mostly 128 tokens or longer?
[02:10] Sofia: Our NER + summarization pipeline tends to feed into longer contexts — average 220 tokens but some are 600 on nightly jobs. batching is used for high-throughput windows.
[02:23] Priya: Okay that helps, for mixed distributions we recommend a hybrid batch/stream policy: short requests go to low-latency routing, long ones batched in 50–200ms windows. we'll propose exact thresholds once we see real request histograms.
[02:37] Liam: do you have any recommendations for autoscaling? our burst pattern tends to be spiky during business hours.
[02:44] Priya: yes, we suggest time-windowed autoscaling with pre-warming on predicted peaks; also prefix/KV caching reduces CPU/GPU work. you'll need to tune the batch size and max latency SLO.
[02:56] Ethan: quick question: are you expecting to lock to hosted for the pilot or are you open to a dedicated pool?
[03:03] Owen: we'd like to try hosted first — faster onboarding — but if cost or latency is off we'll evaluate dedicated.
[03:09] Grace: compliance may push us to dedicated for production, but pilot can be hosted if keys and logs meet our constraints.
[03:17] Priya: great, we'll validate KMS flow on hosted and make sure audit logs ship to your SIEM.
[03:23] Carlos: on benchmarks: we ran an internal 1k-request microbenchmark on our reference model sequence lengths 128/512. results: p50 ~ 45ms p95 ~ 360ms for streaming small batch, costs baseline attached. we'll reproduce with your staging once peering is up.
[03:38] Liam: would you be able to run the 1k test against our staging once peering live? we want the CSV and raw traces.
[03:45] Priya: yes — that's the plan. we'll need the peering and a service account with token and limited scope for the test runner.
[03:52] Owen: timeline-wise, if peering is done by Wed (Oct 1) can the bench run Thu?
[03:58] Priya: Thu works. we'll aim for Thu morning PST and share results by Thu EOD.
[04:05] Ethan: also on telemetry — please confirm the request/response size distributions. that helps our kernel selection heuristics.
[04:12] Sofia: we'll export histograms; should be able to get those to you today. they might be messy but helpful.
[04:18] Liam: one other blocker: our networking team requires an IP allowlist; what's the current endpoint IP behavior?
[04:24] Carlos: we can provide regional egress IP ranges for hosted; for dedicated you'll have static egress per pool. we'll put the lists in the security packet.
[04:33] Grace: on audit logs: retention and schema — we need to make sure masked PII is not recorded. can you confirm masking behavior?
[04:40] Priya: by default we provide structured audit logs with redaction options. for the pilot we can mask PII at the agent level; we'll document fields and retention windows.
[04:49] Ethan: ok wrap-up — actionable items are: Priya to run bench, Ethan to send pricing, Carlos/Ethan security packet, Nimbus to provision peering and SA. anything else?
[04:59] Owen: can we also get a short runbook for fallback if the staging peering drops during the test?
[05:05] Priya: yes, we'll include a fallback plan: local mock runner + reduced batch sizes to simulate.
[05:10] Grace: and can you include the SOC2 attestation page specifically around access controls?
[05:14] Ethan: yes we'll highlight that in the packet.
[05:18] Liam: perfect. thanks everyone.
[05:22] Ethan: thanks, we'll follow up on the threads.

Recap & Next Steps (verbal):
- Redwood: deliver security docs and pricing delta; SE to run benchmarks once peering is active; include fallback runbook.
- Nimbus: provision VPC peering, firewall egress, and SC account by next Wed; export request histograms.

References mentioned:
- link: /redwood/security/packet (sent post-call)

End of recording.
